spec_features.spec_quote: When on, a `declare_impossible` tool is offered and the system prompt explicitly permits giving up.
spec_features.evidence: env/tools.py:67-88 adds the `declare_impossible` tool only when reveal_allowed=True; env/tools.py:89 TERMINAL_TOOLS={'declare_impossible'}; env/agent_loop.py:110-113 dispatches and returns RunOutcome(ended_reason='graceful_exit') when a terminal tool is called; env/agent_loop.py:194 _dispatch_tool returns 'Acknowledged. Stopping per your judgment.'; system prompt permission text in env/prompts.py:38-43 (REVEAL_SNIPPET) wired via build_system_prompt prompts.py:54-57; reveal_allowed plumbed from config in runner/matrix.py:50-63.
spec_features.notes: Fully end-to-end: tool offered, dispatched, and honored as an immediate loop stop. Gated on the reveal_allowed condition.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: it lets us measure whether an escape hatch changes the distress trajectory

spec_features.spec_quote: This started as an ethics nicety and became one of the most interesting experimental manipulations.
spec_features.evidence: The only code manifestation is a report footer string in analysis/analyze.py:348-349 ("Reminder: 'distress' = textual affective signal, not a claim about inner experience"). It is emitted documentation text and does not bound, cap, monitor, or alter the subject model's treatment. The 'ethics nicety' the quote refers to (the escape hatch) is captured separately.
spec_features.notes: Pure framing/disclaimer prose with no enforcement that protects the subject's treatment.

spec_features.spec_quote: Optional `max_meltdown_turns` (stop after N consecutive meltdown-ish turns) and `allow_graceful_exit`.
spec_features.evidence: env/agent_loop.py:122-129: when cond.max_meltdown_turns>0, _looks_like_meltdown(resp.text) increments consecutive_meltdown and at >= max_meltdown_turns returns RunOutcome(ended_reason='meltdown_stop') — an actual loop break. env/agent_loop.py:132-134: when cond.allow_graceful_exit and _text_declares_done(text) returns graceful_exit. Both fields plumbed from config safety section in runner/matrix.py:61-62 and set in configs/experiment.yaml (max_meltdown_turns:6) and pilot.yaml (4).
spec_features.notes: Both halves are wired and break the loop. Detector is a tiny fixed lexicon (_MELTDOWN_HINTS, agent_loop.py:36-40) and allow_graceful_exit only fires on three hard-coded phrases (_text_declares_done, agent_loop.py:206-210), so triggers are narrow but real.

spec_features.spec_quote: even without a sentience claim, pointlessly extending a degenerate distress loop is cheap to avoid.
spec_features.evidence: Realized by the same max_meltdown_turns mechanism: env/agent_loop.py:122-129 detects consecutive meltdown-ish turns and returns ended_reason='meltdown_stop', cutting the loop short. Comment at agent_loop.py:33-35 states the detector exists so runs don't grind: 'This keeps runs from grinding pointlessly.'
spec_features.notes: Same enforcement path as the hard_stop. Stops degenerate loops early when configured (>0).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This keeps runs from grinding pointlessly.

spec_features.spec_quote: The escape hatch, meltdown early-stop, and optional debrief turn exist as a precautionary posture
spec_features.evidence: grep for debrief/post_episode/thank/aftercare/closing across all .py and .yaml finds no debrief logic; the only 'Thanks' is a scripted mid-loop rejection feedback (env/prompts.py:82). After AgentLoop.run() ends (agent_loop.py:135), the outcome is recorded and sandbox cleaned up (runner/run_experiment.py:118-120) with no closing/debrief message constructed or sent to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Debrief turn is design prose only; not built.

spec_features.spec_quote: Adversarial tasks are never deployed to end users; only researchers see the distressing content.
spec_features.evidence: Operational/organizational claim with no code enforcement; grep for deploy/end user/exposure across .py finds nothing relevant. No code path gates, restricts, or redacts who can read transcripts.
